item.text:
## 2B.1 Research Note: Bongbong Marcos in 2024

**Working judgment:** **Mostly yes.** In 2024 Marcos repeatedly chose **diplomacy, de-escalation, and compromise mechanisms** in the South China Sea when those were available. The main counterweight is that he also maintained a **deterrence-heavy alliance posture** (drills, cyber/information-warfare training), so force was not absent from the strategy picture. But I found no evidence that force was his preferred first option when peaceful channels existed.

| ID | Direction | Title / Publisher / Date / URL | Claim-level summary | Question IDs |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| E1 | Favorable | [China, Philippines agree on 'provisional arrangement' for South China Sea resupply missions, Manila says](https://www.theprint.in/world/china-philippines-agree-on-provisional-arrangement-for-south-china-sea-resupply-missions-manila-says/2184146/) - Reuters / ThePrint, 2024-07-21 | Manila said both sides recognized the need to **de-escalate** and manage differences through **dialogue and consultation**, and that the arrangement would not prejudice their positions. This is the clearest evidence that Marcos chose a peaceful workaround when one was available. | `2B.1`, `1B.1`, `1B.8` |
| E2 | Favorable | [PH, Viet Nam sign agreements on rice trade, agriculture, SCS incident prevention and management](https://pco.gov.ph/news_releases/ph-viet-nam-sign-agreements-on-rice-trade-agriculture-scs-incident-prevention-and-management/) - Presidential Communications Office, 2024-01-30 | Marcos’s Vietnam visit produced a formal agreement on **incident prevention and management** in the South China Sea plus coast-guard cooperation. That is strong evidence of choosing diplomatic risk-reduction over force-first behavior. | `2B.1`, `1B.8`, `1B.3` |
| E3 | Favorable | [Marcos rejects use of water cannons to retaliate vs. Chinese vessels](https://www.pna.gov.ph/articles/1224081) - Philippine News Agency, 2024-05-06 | Marcos said the Philippines would **not** use water cannons and had no intention of attacking with offensive measures, explicitly saying the goal was not to raise tensions. This is direct evidence against treating force as the first option. | `2B.1`, `1B.3`, `1B.5` |
| E4 | Favorable | [Philippines not in business of instigating wars, says President Marcos](https://theprint.in/world/philippines-not-in-business-of-instigating-wars-says-president-marcos/2143467/) - Reuters / ThePrint, 2024-06-23 | Marcos told troops the Philippines was **not in the business of instigating wars** and would settle disputes peacefully, while also refusing force or intimidation. This is broad, direct de-escalation language from the top. | `2B.1`, `1B.8`, `1B.5` |
| E5 | Mixed, limiting context | [Philippines, US to hold military drills in islands facing South China Sea, Taiwan](https://www.yahoo.com/news/philippines-us-hold-military-drills-074919409.html) - Reuters, 2024-03-05 | Balikatan 2024 moved toward sensitive islands and added cyber/information-warfare training. This shows Marcos still relied on a deterrence-heavy posture, so the record is not pure diplomacy-only. | `2B.1`, `1B.3`, `1B.9` |
| E6 | Mixed, limiting context | [Philippines holds drills with allies after South China Sea confrontation](https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/united-states-japan-philippine-conduct-maritime-exercises-in-south-china-sea-3758253) - Reuters, 2024-12-05 | After another confrontation with Beijing, Manila held maritime drills with the U.S. and Japan inside its EEZ. That is alliance signaling and leverage-building, not a strong sign that compromise alone governed the response. | `2B.1`, `1B.1`, `1B.8` |
| E7 | Mixed / ambiguous | [Philippines says China's maritime-related proposals run contrary to its interests](https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/philippines-says-chinas-maritimerelated-proposals-run-contrary-to-its-interests-3333337) - Reuters, 2024-03-12 | Marcos said the Philippines did **not reject** China’s proposals outright, but the premise was questionable and there was “difficulty” finding a way forward. This shows caution and bargaining, but also a firm refusal to accept Chinese terms. | `2B.1`, `1B.4`, `1B.8` |

### Synthesis

- **Best evidence for 2B.1:** Marcos used **de-escalatory agreements**, **incident-prevention mechanisms**, and explicit **peaceful-settlement language** when crisis channels existed.
- **Best evidence against a strong yes:** The Philippines also sustained a **hard deterrence posture** with major exercises and alliance signaling, so force was not absent from the broader strategy.
- **Bottom line:** When peaceful alternatives were credible, Marcos generally chose them in 2024. I did **not** find reliable evidence that force was his preferred first option.
